newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Aid workers arrested in Kabul - relief official.
newsitem.headline: Aid workers arrested in Kabul - relief official.

text.p: At least 12 aid workers, all Afghan nationals, have been arrested by the Taleban authorities in Kabul on charges of gun running, a relief official said on Sunday.
"At least 12 aid organisation employees were arrested last Tuesday. The staff have been accused of gun running." said Ross Everson of the Agency Coordinating Body for Afghan Relief, an umbrella body.

He said that the arrested workers, all men, were from three aid organisations: the French-based Afghan Vaccination and Immunisation center (Avicen), and locally based organisations Development and Humanitarian Services for Afghanistan (DHSA) and Coordination of Humanitarian Assistance.
Avicen and DHSA were also accused as organisations of involvement in gun running, he said.
According to Everson, the men were arrested by the 1st Army Division, but he said he had been unable to find out what had become of them.

"We are doing our utmost to find out what has happened to these men. We have seen the 1st Army Division, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Security Ministry, but they either do not know what is happening or they are not saying." said Everson.
Everson said that he would continue to try to find out what had happened to the men.
On February 21 seven employees of the French aid organisation Action Contre la Faim (Action against Hunger) were arrested by the Taleban authorities and accused of immoral behavior.
They have all been released after serving varying sentences, some of which included a symbolic whipping.
